## Recommended headline

**Swarm: one chat runs Codex, Gemini and Claude Code on your project at once (Beta)**

It names real agents, can't be mistaken for one vendor's own subagents, and stays true as phase 2 ships. Alternatives: "Swarm: hand jobs to other agents and get their work on main with one click to undo" (sells the merge), or "Swarm: a team of agents from every provider, on your own PC" (vaguer).

## Release-notes entry (beta.10)

#### Swarm (Beta): one chat runs helpers from every provider, and their work lands on main with Undo

Splitting a job across agents meant a chat per agent, a brief for each and merging every branch yourself. Now you ask one chat, and its agent starts helpers from Codex, Claude Code, Gemini or any other agent you've turned on, each in its own copy of the project. Helpers report back into your chat, and each merge shows one line, such as Merged "Fix login bug" (Codex) into main · 3 commits, with **Undo** and **Merge again**. Only the main agent merges, at most 3 helpers run per project, no two helpers own the same files, and it all runs on your PC with no AIB cloud.

## Feature page

**Intro.** Your web app has a login bug, a slow search page and a signup form with no tests. You could open three chats with three agents, write three briefs, watch three windows and merge three branches by hand. Or you tell one chat: "Have Codex fix the login bug, Gemini speed up search, and add signup tests yourself." The main agent starts each helper in its own copy of the project. Helpers report back into your chat, and their work lands on main one line at a time, each with an **Undo** button.

### Cross-agent helpers: the right agent for each job, from one chat

Any agent you've set up in AIB can be a helper: a Claude Code chat can send work to Codex, a Codex chat to Claude Code. Give each job to the agent that's good at it, or the one that still has plan left, without leaving your chat. Each helper uses its own CLI and your own sign-in for that provider. ✎ Claude helpers are on by default; you can turn them off.

### Own copy per helper: helpers never touch your folder or each other

Every helper works in its own git worktree and branch, started from main. No agent edits your project folder directly, so the file open in your editor doesn't change under you. Two running helpers can't own the same files.

### Reports in your chat: no tab-hopping to see what helpers did

When a helper finishes, a report lands in your main chat: files changed, lines added and removed, and commits, counted by AIB itself, plus what the helper says it did. ✎ Each helper is told to run its own tests and say whether they passed; AIB shows that result as the helper's word, not its own check. Each helper is also a chat of its own you can open.

### One-line merges with Undo: helpers' work lands on main, and one click takes it back

> Merged "Fix login bug" (Codex) into main · 3 commits **Undo**

✎ **Undo** adds one commit that takes the merge back out of main; nothing is rewritten. **Merge again** puts it back. If later work changed the same lines, Undo says so and changes nothing. If main moved on before the merge, the helper's copy is brought up to date first; if that clashes, the helper is asked to fix it before anything lands.

### Guards: helpers can't merge themselves, multiply or step on each other

- **Only the main agent merges.** A helper can't merge its own work into main.
- **Helpers can't start helpers.** One level only.
- **At most 3 helpers per project** at a time.
- **No shared files** between running helpers.
- **Nobody edits your folder.** Every agent works in its own copy.
- ✎ **Your edits are safe.** Uncommitted changes in your project folder are set aside during a merge or Undo and put back after.

### Local: your PC, your agents, no AIB cloud

Helpers run on your PC as the same CLIs you already use. AIB has no cloud service, account or servers in between; your prompts and code go only to the providers of the agents you use.

### How it works

1. **Ask in your chat**, e.g. "Have Codex fix the login bug and Claude write the settings page."
2. **The main agent starts the helpers**, each in its own copy, with a brief and the files it owns.
3. **Helpers work** in their own copies at the same time.
4. **Helpers report back** into your chat.
5. **The main agent merges** each helper's work; each merge posts one line with **Undo**.

### What's not built yet

Swarm is Beta. Planned, not shipped: helpers grouped under the main chat in the sidebar (for now each is its own chat); one inbox entry for a whole swarm (for now helpers notify like any chat); a Helpers strip; helper labels on the phone. Swarm needs a git project, because helpers work in worktrees.
